title: Waiting for Ellington at the Lafayette Theater
summary: Arriving in Harlem, he waits for Ellington's return and sits through the Lafayette Theater's multiple daily shows.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: I got into New York, and Duke Ellington was out of town. So I wait until the band got back. The day that --
He was traveling. Duke Ellington went to the road.

So I waited until they got back. And I never forget they opened Lafayette Theater. That was on Seventh Avenue and 132nd, 131st. That was when the -- the big Black shows, every week they had to deal with a new show, different orchestra.
Yeah, in late '30s. I got into the theater when they opened at 9:00 o'clock in the morning. And I stay there until they finally show up (inaudible) that night.
They started back at 9:00 in the morning?
